title: Effect of the use of Mechanical AutoTransfusion on postpartum red blood cell volume in women following elective caesarean section without an increased risk of bleeding
summary:
On average, approximately 500–1,000 ml of blood is lost during caesarean section deliveries. Blood loss exceeding 1,000 ml is classified as peripartum haemorrhage and occurs in 5–10 per cent of procedures, leading to an increased risk of morbidity and the need for blood transfusions. Mechanical autotransfusion (MAT) can reduce the need for blood transfusions in cases of severe peripartum haemorrhage, and professional bodies recommend it as a safe component of patient blood management [3, 14]. 
However, the benefits of its routine use in improving objectively measured haemoglobin concentration, calculated haematocrit and mothers’ subjective postnatal well-being, particularly in elective caesarean sections, are currently the subject of debate [1–5]. This study aims to investigate whether intraoperative MAT during elective caesarean sections leads to increased erythrocyte volume postoperatively (compared to caesarean sections without MAT). The study will also investigate whether a reduction in anaemia-related side effects could enhance women’s subjective physical and psychological resilience following childbirth, thereby improving breastfeeding behaviour and postnatal well-being. MAT is recommended by professional bodies as a safe and effective measure in patient blood management during caesarean section deliveries, and it has been used at Augsburg University Hospital for many years. Although there are theoretical risks, such as incorrect transfusion or alloimmunisation, these are considered to be very low due to the physical separation of the procedures and the available study data. Participation in the study does not increase these risks.  [4, 20, 21].
conditions: Anaemia during pregnancy and the postnatal period

interventions.name: Current standard procedure without MAT for elective caesarean sections without an increased risk of bleeding
New standard procedure using MAT for elective caesarean sections without an increased risk of bleeding

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Women who undergo an elective caesarean section without an increased risk of bleeding
Exclusion criteria:
•    Increased risk of bleeding, e.g. placenta accreta spectrum, known coagulation disorder, e.g. haemophilia
•    Refusal to participate in the study
•    Inability to give informed consent
•    Participation in another interventional study
•    Pre-existing congenital heart conditions
•    Pre-existing haematological conditions or haemolytic anaemia
•    Refusal of MAT (e.g. Jehovah’s Witnesses)
•    Allergy to heparin
